objective: Give the release manifest one unambiguous verdict per question — provenance completeness, promotion eligibility, publication — so no artifact reads as release-eligible while the promotion predicate refuses it.
decision_supported: Should release_eligible follow provenance completeness or promotion, and can downstream readers be migrated without losing the weaker signal?
acceptance: The manifest carries provenance_complete, promotion_eligible and release_eligible, and release_eligible equals promotion_eligible.
promotion_eligible is false for an unsigned, unverifiable or failed-attestation manifest.
provenance_reasons and promotion_reasons are written so a reader knows which question was refused.
A test asserts the invariant over every attestation status.
The documentation distinguishes the three questions.
Existing readers of release_eligible keep a field with that name, now narrower than before.
evidence: The issue probe: verify_manifest returns () while promotion_reasons returns the attestation reason, and the old manifest still wrote release_eligible: true.
After the change the same probe reports provenance_complete True, promotion_eligible False, release_eligible False, and both flip together when the attestation becomes signed.
The pre-existing test asserted release_eligible was true for an unsigned manifest; it now asserts the three fields separately.
stop_conditions: A consumer is found that treats release_eligible as provenance completeness and cannot be told apart; that would need an explicit migration note rather than the alias.
risks_and_fallbacks: This makes release_eligible false where it was true, which is the point of the issue but is a breaking change for any reader; the name is preserved and the reasons are now in the manifest.
The workflow still writes an unsigned manifest at build time; it is now labelled as provenance-complete rather than release-eligible.
